# Grove — web front end

The browser surface for [Grove](../README.md): a fleet of agent workspaces, each one a git worktree plus a tmux session, on this host or inside a container.

It talks to the Grove daemon over the same OpenAPI contract the CLI, the TUI and the MCP server use. It owns no wire format of its own, and it holds no state the daemon is not already the source of truth for.

---

## The one rule

**Every visual component here is generated by `assistant-ui add` or `shadcn add` and committed verbatim. Grove code composes them and never restyles them.**

`components/{assistant-ui,elements,ui,icons}/` is upstream source we happen to store; `components/grove/` is the only hand-written tree. A gate enforces this rather than a convention: `registry:check` re-fetches every vendored file and fails on any drift, and `lint:styling` fails on colour, radius or shadow utilities under `components/grove/`.

Two documents govern work here, and they are worth reading before the code:

- **[`design-system.md`](design-system.md)** — the type scale, the neutral text ramp, monospace and numeric rules, the semantic colour palette, button and badge taxonomies, the entity glyph map, card and table patterns, and the states every surface must handle. Prescriptive and token-named: you should be able to build a new screen from it without asking anyone.
- **[`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md)** — the engineering contract and the hard-won specifics, including why the shell is a hand-rolled rail rather than shadcn's `Sidebar`, which files are declared ports of vendored components, and the measurement lessons behind the performance work.

---

## Running it

Needs **Node 22 or newer** (Next 16). The repo's Make targets are the supported entry points and resolve this directory for you:

```bash
make webapp-dev                       # dev server
make webapp-build                     # production build
make webapp-gate                      # typecheck, drift, styling, tests
```

`GROVE_DAEMON_URL` points at the daemon (default `http://127.0.0.1:7421`). There is no model provider key: the browser never talks to an LLM, only to the daemon.

> [!TIP]
> In production this serves a **pre-built** `.next` under systemd, so a merge is invisible until you rebuild and restart. Building under a running server also breaks it — the live process keeps the old manifest and every dynamic route 500s with `ChunkLoadError`. One owner builds and restarts.

---

## Layout

```
app/            routes only — thin, no logic
components/
  assistant-ui/ ┐
  elements/     ├ VENDORED, verbatim
  ui/           │
  icons/        ┘
  grove/        the only hand-written components
lib/grove/
  api/          generated types + typed client — ALL network I/O
  adapters/     PURE: wire shape → assistant-ui props
  runtime/      ExternalStoreRuntime + thread-list wiring
  hooks/        react-query + the SSE subscription
```

Dependencies flow inward. The adapters are pure so they are testable without a daemon — that is the acceptance criterion for the layer, not a stylistic preference.

`useExternalStoreRuntime` is the correct runtime here because the daemon hands over complete message lists via REST and SSE rather than streaming tokens; freshness comes from the event stream, and every `refetchInterval` is a backstop that switches off while the stream is healthy.

---

## Gates

`npm run gate` runs them in order: `typecheck` → `check:ignored` → `registry:check` → `lint:styling` → `test`. Playwright (`npm run test:e2e`) is separate and owns its own port.

`registry:check` needs network — the upstream registry is the oracle. `check:ignored` exists because the repo's Python `lib/` ignore rule once swallowed this app's whole data layer while `git add` said nothing.
